questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?
questions.explanation: The story focuses on Lina finding her way and beginning to feel at home.
options: Lina uses a map and a friendly meeting place to feel more comfortable at a new school.
Lina loses her brother’s map and cannot find her classroom.
Sam teaches Lina how to draw a perfect map of the school.
The school fountain breaks during Lina’s first day.
questions.correct_answer: Lina uses a map and a friendly meeting place to feel more comfortable at a new school.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What did Lina add to the map by the end of the day?
questions.explanation: The final paragraph states that she added these two marks.
options: A circle around her classroom and a small leaf beside the fountain
A list of homework tasks and the lunch menu
A drawing of every student in her class
A warning about the busy corridors
questions.correct_answer: A circle around her classroom and a small leaf beside the fountain

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the school no longer feel unknown to Lina?
questions.explanation: The map, classroom, fountain, and Sam help Lina feel more settled.
options: She has found familiar places and made a friendly connection.
She has memorised every corridor in the building.
Her brother comes to guide her through the school.
The school becomes smaller during the day.
questions.correct_answer: She has found familiar places and made a friendly connection.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In the first paragraph, what does "important" suggest about the doors?
questions.explanation: Lina is new, so the doors feel significant and unfamiliar.
options: They seem to lead to places Lina needs to understand.
They are painted in bright colours.
They are locked and cannot be opened.
They are much heavier than ordinary doors.
questions.correct_answer: They seem to lead to places Lina needs to understand.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the author include the star on the map?
questions.explanation: The star marks the fountain, a helpful meeting place.
options: To show a place that helps Lina feel less lost
To explain where the lunch hall is located
To show that Lina dislikes using maps
To mark a place that students must avoid
questions.correct_answer: To show a place that helps Lina feel less lost

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: How does the story change from beginning to end?
questions.explanation: Lina starts lost and ends with the school feeling more familiar.
options: It moves from uncertainty to growing confidence.
It moves from excitement to serious danger.
It moves from a group project to a private argument.
It moves from a finished day to an earlier morning.
questions.correct_answer: It moves from uncertainty to growing confidence.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
questions.explanation: The whole text explains how a small window garden supports observation.
options: A window garden helps students observe plant growth in a small space.
A window garden is the fastest way to grow a large harvest.
Plants should always be kept away from sunlight.
Students need an outdoor field to learn about plants.
questions.correct_answer: A window garden helps students observe plant growth in a small space.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why are small stones placed at the bottom of the tray?
questions.explanation: The text says stones help extra water drain away.
options: To help extra water drain away
To stop sunlight reaching the seeds
To make the tray too heavy to move
To keep the leaves below the soil
questions.correct_answer: To help extra water drain away

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What would probably happen if the soil were soaked every day?
questions.explanation: The text contrasts careful watering with too much watering.
options: The plants might not grow as well because they receive too much water.
The plants would immediately produce a large harvest.
The seeds would turn into stones.
The tray would no longer need sunlight.
questions.correct_answer: The plants might not grow as well because they receive too much water.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What does "observe" mean in this text?
questions.explanation: Students measure, sketch, and note changes, so observe means watch carefully.
options: Watch carefully and record what happens
Move something to a new place
questions.correct_answer: Watch carefully and record what happens

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why did the author write this text?
questions.explanation: The text gives instructions and explains learning benefits.
options: To explain how a small garden can be used for learning
To tell a funny story about a gardener
To persuade readers to stop eating vegetables
To describe the history of school windows
questions.correct_answer: To explain how a small garden can be used for learning

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: How is the text mainly organised?
questions.explanation: The text first gives setup steps, then explains observations and learning.
options: It explains steps and then describes what students can learn.
It compares five different schools in order.
It lists problems without giving solutions.
It tells events in a mystery story.
questions.correct_answer: It explains steps and then describes what students can learn.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the explanation?
questions.explanation: The explanation is about how folded shape increases strength.
options: Folding paper changes its shape and can make it stronger.
Coins are always lighter than paper.
Books should not be used in science tests.
Wood and metal are weaker than paper.
questions.correct_answer: Folding paper changes its shape and can make it stronger.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What happened to the flat paper bridge in the class test?
questions.explanation: The passage states that the flat bridge sagged almost immediately.
options: It held all the coins easily.
It turned into a folded bridge by itself.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why did each group place the books the same distance apart?
questions.explanation: Keeping the gap the same controls an important part of the test.
options: To make the test fair for each bridge
To make the books easier to read
To stop the coins from being counted
questions.correct_answer: To make the test fair for each bridge

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What does "sagged" mean in the passage?
questions.explanation: A bridge that sags bends downward under weight.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the author mention engineers?
questions.explanation: The engineer example shows how shape matters in real structures.
options: To connect the classroom test to real design work
To say only engineers can fold paper
To explain that students should build metal bridges
To change the topic to bicycles only
questions.correct_answer: To connect the classroom test to real design work

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence best describes the final paragraph?
questions.explanation: The final paragraph states the lesson and connects it to real objects.
options: It explains what the test proved and gives real-world examples.
It introduces the characters and setting.
It lists all the materials needed in order.
It argues that paper is always the best building material.
questions.correct_answer: It explains what the test proved and gives real-world examples.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly describing?
questions.explanation: Most details describe the courtyard after rain.
options: A school courtyard changing after rain
A football match during a storm
A music lesson inside a classroom
A group of students planting flowers
questions.correct_answer: A school courtyard changing after rain

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What moved around the fallen flower petal?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions ants moving around the petal.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the football wait under the shelter?
questions.explanation: The text says it waits for the ground to dry.
options: The ground is still too wet for play.
No one at the school likes football.
The football has been lost for many weeks.
The music room is using it for a lesson.
questions.correct_answer: The ground is still too wet for play.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What does "flashed silver" suggest about the puddles?
questions.explanation: The sun makes the puddles shine brightly.
options: They reflected bright light from the sun.
They were filled with metal coins.
questions.correct_answer: They reflected bright light from the sun.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the writer use many sensory details?
questions.explanation: Smells, sounds, sights, and movement create a vivid description.
options: To help the reader imagine the quiet courtyard clearly
To give instructions for cleaning the courtyard
To explain how rain clouds form
questions.correct_answer: To help the reader imagine the quiet courtyard clearly

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: How is the description organised?
questions.explanation: The scene changes over time from quiet after rain to students returning.
options: It moves from immediately after the rain to when the sun and students return.
It gives instructions in numbered steps.
It presents a problem and then a letter of complaint.
It compares indoor and outdoor sports equally.
questions.correct_answer: It moves from immediately after the rain to when the sun and students return.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What is the notice mainly about?
questions.explanation: The notice explains the team and how students can join.
options: Inviting students to join and help the school library team
Announcing that the library will close every Wednesday
Explaining why students must stop borrowing books
Listing every book in the school library
questions.correct_answer: Inviting students to join and help the school library team

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: When does the library team meet?
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives the meeting time.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which student would likely be a good team member?
questions.explanation: The notice says members should be reliable, careful, and willing to listen.
options: A student who listens, is careful, and likes helping quietly
A student who wants to hide books from others
A student who refuses to work with anyone
A student who only wants to play loud games
questions.correct_answer: A student who listens, is careful, and likes helping quietly

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: What does "reliable" mean in the notice?
questions.explanation: Reliable means dependable or trustworthy.
options: Able to be trusted to do what is needed
questions.correct_answer: Able to be trusted to do what is needed

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Why does the notice say joining is not only for strong readers?
questions.explanation: The notice wants students with different helpful skills to feel welcome.
options: To encourage different kinds of helpful students to join
To stop strong readers from joining the team
To explain that books are not important in the library
To warn students that the work is too difficult

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: How does the notice build its message?
questions.explanation: The paragraphs move from duties to joining details to encouragement.
options: It explains the team’s tasks, gives joining instructions, then describes who may enjoy it.
It tells a story with a surprise ending.
It compares two libraries in different countries.
It begins with a conclusion and then gives a poem.
